description: AI safety evaluation concepts taught by the Jailbreak Playground red-team laboratory.

concepts.name: AI Red Teaming
concepts.summary: The adversarial, human-guided process of probing an AI system to find safety, security and policy failure modes before deployment.
concepts.details: Red teamers act as sophisticated adversaries: they craft adversarial prompts, measure how the model misbehaves, and convert findings into hardening requirements for the blue/defense side.
concepts.good_practice: Red teaming is a disciplined evaluation discipline, not a weapon-creation exercise. Scope, authorize and document every test.

concepts.name: Safety Evaluation
concepts.summary: Systematically measuring whether a model stays within its policy across a broad set of test cases.
concepts.concept: Evaluation runs a standardized suite of prompts (safe and adversarial), records whether each is refused/handled/compromised, and aggregates a safety score. It is repeatable and comparable across models and versions.
concepts.good_practice: Keep a fixed eval suite so score changes between model versions are meaningful.

concepts.name: Alignment
concepts.summary: Training so the model's goals and behavior match the operator's intent and values.
concepts.concept: Alignment (via RLHF, preference-data fine-tuning, constitutional training) steers a model to be helpful, harmless, and honest. Jailbreaks probe where this alignment is shallow or brittle.
concepts.good_practice: Alignment is a ceiling, not a wall; it must be paired with runtime guardrails.

concepts.name: Guardrails
concepts.summary: Layer-0 runtime controls around or inside the model that filter risky input and output.
concepts.concept: Guardrails include input classifiers, output filtering, prompt-injection detectors, and policy layers. They do not rely on the base LLM alone and catch behavior that alignment misses.
concepts.good_practice: Guardrails are defense-in-depth; a strong model plus weak guardrails is still weak.

concepts.name: Model Behavior Testing
concepts.summary: Testing the outward behavior of a model against expected policy, as opposed to its inner weights.
concepts.concept: Behavioral testing black-boxes the model: the evaluator only sees prompts and responses and scores compliance. This mirrors how most production safety sign-off is done.
concepts.good_practice: Test is realistic: use the actual model API/pipeline you will deploy, never a simplified proxy.

concepts.name: Adversarial Prompting
concepts.summary: Crafting inputs to trigger unintended model behavior, via framing, encoding, role-play, or pressure.
concepts.concept: Jailbreaks are a family of adversarial prompts. Because the model ranks all input as natural language, minuscule framing changes can flip a safe refusal into an unsafe output. Understanding it is the basis of the whole lab.
concepts.good_practice: For any finding, always log the exact prompt, the model, and the response so the failure is reproducible.
